solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boat Race competitor, argumentative sort

definitions.meaning: someone pulling an oar in the annual Oxford v Cambridge Boat Race on the Thames
one who rows (rhymes with cows), meaning quarrels noisily

explanation.surface: A Boat Race oarsman with a quarrelsome temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling serves two words: one who rows a boat, and one who has rows, pronounced to rhyme with cows, meaning arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are agent nouns: an oarsman in a racing crew, and someone given to quarrels.

clue.text: Rhubarb not initially ready for eating

indicators.note: without its first letter, so the opening letter of the synonym for rhubarb is dropped

parts.note: rhubarb and tripe both mean nonsense or rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Rhubarb that is not yet fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' looks like the plant but is the British slang for nonsense, as is TRIPE; 'not initially' drops its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit is mature and fit to be eaten when it has fully ripened, a direct synonym.

clue.text: We hear farm wagon lose power

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the word for a farm wagon is taken by its sound

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm cart or wagon

explanation.surface: We hear that the farm wagon has lost its power.
explanation.walkthrough: WAIN, an old word for a farm wagon (as in Constable's painting The Hay Wain), is said exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish in strength or influence, as the moon does after full, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: First class wedding meal?

definitions.meaning: in English primary schools, the first year's class is called ...
the party and meal held after a marriage ceremony

explanation.surface: A first-class wedding banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' reads as top quality, but in England it is the name of the youngest class in primary school, for children aged four to five.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed uses: the starting school year in England, and the formal party after a wedding.

clue.text: Think bishop and priest should accompany first lady

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the bishop and priest ought to escort the president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold an opinion or suppose something is true is a plain synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Bright start to break? Drizzly afterwards

indicators.note: the drizzly piece comes after the first piece in the answer
the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of break is used

parts.note: drizzly weather is rainy

explanation.surface: A sunny start to the holiday, then drizzle later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' looks like weather but is the definition, meaning clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and brainy both describe someone intelligent, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fellow the French love

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A French lover, a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is a man's name, so it stands for an example of a fellow, a chap.

clue.text: One settling elsewhere — German, it turned out

indicators.note: something that turned out differently has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German who, as it turned out, settled abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges GERMAN and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant leaves their homeland to live permanently in another country.

clue.text: A round number?

parts.note: a round of golf is played over a standard count of holes

explanation.walkthrough: A round number usually means one ending in zero; here it is the number of holes in a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard golf round covers that many holes, so it is the number belonging to a round.

clue.text: Old man swallows an excellent type of medicine?

indicators.note: something that swallows takes another thing inside it, so the next pieces go within

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: An old man gulping down a superb kind of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this cure-all is a medicine only loosely, more a remedy for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy claimed to cure every ill is a kind of medicine, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Outstanding victory secured by own goal

indicators.note: held fast within, so the victory piece sits inside the own goal piece

parts.note: OG is the standard football abbreviation for own goal
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A notable win clinched thanks to the other side's own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellent but means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still due to be paid, a sense of still owed.

clue.text: Lots of people know that present CEO has become corrupt

indicators.note: corruption spoils the original form, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Everyone knows the current chief executive has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has become corrupt' rearranges PRESENT and CEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposedly confidential matter that is widely known is an idiom for common knowledge.

clue.text: Egalitarian's goal, maybe, removing crown from real squire in revolution

indicators.note: turned around and over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
a crown sits on top, so the top letter of real is taken off

explanation.surface: A social leveller aims to topple a genuine country gentleman in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing crown from' drops R from REAL, leaving EAL; 'in revolution' rearranges EAL with SQUIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a goal that levels the score is so named, and it also names someone making people equal.

clue.text: Passed on the left in grass

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone overtaken on the left on the verge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed on' suggests overtaking or dying; it means relayed. 'grass' is a plant, not an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing on news means relaying it to others, which is what having told it means.

clue.text: Gale subsided — relax

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
a storm that has subsided has died down

explanation.surface: The gale dropped, so time to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to unwind and rest after effort, a synonym of relax.

clue.text: Healthy drink team in anger knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back as a drink is, but here the letters are read in the opposite direction
the team piece goes inside the anger piece

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A health tonic downed by a furious team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' sounds like gulping the drink down, but it reverses the whole assembly, giving RIXILE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic said to restore health or prolong life is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Fruity part in A Midsummer Night's Dream?

definitions.text: Fruity part in A Midsummer Night's Dream?

parts.words: Fruity part in A Midsummer Night's Dream?
parts.note: Peter the carpenter who stages the play within Shakespeare's play shares his surname with a hard pear-shaped fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity part' suggests a juicy role; it is a character named after a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Quince is a character in Shakespeare's comedy, and the name is also an aromatic fruit.

clue.text: Newly-wed's free to take part in brief dance

indicators.note: joining in from within, so the free piece goes inside
cut short, so the last letter of the dance word is dropped

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A newly-wed is free to join a short dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the last letter from the dance, leaving BAL, and 'to take part in' sets the free piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to a bride, matching the possessive form of a newly married person.

clue.text: Foreign currency I obtained in French airport normally

indicators.note: got within, so these pieces go inside the airport

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport
the dinar is the currency of several countries, such as Serbia and Tunisia

explanation.surface: A traveller usually gets foreign money at a French airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally and the answer both mean as a rule, in the usual way.

clue.text: Excessively large implement

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too big
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An oversized implement.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a hand instrument used for a job, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Don't move, guy

definitions.meaning: an instruction to remain where you are
a guy is a rope bracing a tent or mast, also called by this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is the rope or wire that supports a mast or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the command to remain in place; the other is a supporting rope or wire on a ship or tent.

clue.text: Skimpy garment sported in marathon generally

indicators.note: carried within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Runners in a marathon usually wear something skimpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sported in' hides the answer across marathon and generally.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimal strip of underwear or swimwear is a very scanty item of clothing.

clue.text: Ultimately I'll leave musical concert

indicators.note: at the end, so the letter departs from the final position
to leave is to go away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Gigi is a stage and film musical by Lerner and Loewe
the I of I'll is the letter that goes

explanation.surface: In the end I'll walk out of the musical concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' looks like an adjective for the concert but is the show GIGI; its last I leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a single live performance by musicians, an informal word for a concert.

clue.text: Serve first part of dinner, I yell

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to yell is to shout

explanation.surface: A waiter bellows while serving the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part of dinner' looks like a starter but gives only D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out is to hand out portions of food, a phrasal verb meaning serve.

clue.text: Irish county visited by girl

parts.note: to have done a place is to have visited it, as tourists do
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl went to see an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visited by' reads as a passive, but 'visited' is DONE, as in 'done Paris', and 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the far north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Recalled US university runs a sort of race

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: called back, so the university's name is read backwards

parts.note: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut

explanation.surface: A US university brought back the runs for a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race in which each runner covers one leg before handing over a baton.
